fitz_curator.text: The Fitzwilliam was founded in 1816, when Viscount Fitzwilliam left the university his paintings, his books and his music, and the money to build somewhere to put them.
We have Egyptian coffins, Greek pots, Roman coins, Monet, Titian and a great many teacups. Free to come in, which is the best kind of price.

fitz_attendant.text: In 2006 a visitor tripped on an untied shoelace, fell down the stairs and landed on three Chinese vases from the Qing dynasty. Smashed into hundreds of pieces.
The conservators glued every bit back together. The vases are on show again, behind glass now. The staircase has a small, quiet reputation.
So: shoelaces. I'm not saying anything. I'm just looking at yours.

fitz_child.text: Miss says the lions outside the front are guarding the museum. My mate says at night they come down and drink from the gutters.
There's an old Cambridge story that when the lions hear the clock strike midnight, they do exactly that. I'm staying till midnight. Miss says I'm not.
